title: Sri Lankan-Born Melbourne Teen Dineth Fernando, 14, Wins World Youth Scrabble Championship
excerpt: The youngest champion in years beat 218 competitors from across the globe in Nairobi, crediting a daily regimen of memorizing 200 words from the official Scrabble dictionary.
body:
• Dineth Fernando, 14, a Sri Lankan-born teenager representing Australia, won the 2026 World Youth Scrabble Championship in Nairobi, Kenya, beating out 218 competitors from dozens of countries.
  • Fernando moved to Melbourne from Sri Lanka less than a year ago and credits his victory to practising 200 words a day from the official Scrabble dictionary.
  • India's Suyash Manchali finished as second runner-up, continuing a strong run of South Asian success at the tournament, following Madhav Gopal Kamath's title-winning campaign in 2025.
  • Fernando had already made waves on the Australian domestic circuit, averaging 509 points per game at a Victorian regional — a new national record for 2026.

Dineth Fernando was sitting in Nairobi's Trademark Hotel this month, tiles spread before him, when he sealed a victory that had been months in the making. The 14-year-old, who moved to Melbourne from Sri Lanka less than a year ago, is the 2026 World Youth Scrabble Champion.

The tournament, held August 7 to 9, drew 218 young players from countries spanning six continents. Fernando, competing under the Australian flag, topped the field ahead of England's Samuel Crispin in second place and India's Suyash Manchali in third.

From Colombo to Melbourne to Nairobi

Fernando's path to the world title began on the competitive Scrabble circuit in Sri Lanka, where he cut his teeth at events like the All Island Open Scrabble Championship and junior nationals organized by the Sri Lanka Scrabble League. He relocated to Melbourne in late 2025 and quickly established himself in Victoria's senior competitive scene.

At a regional tournament in Ballarat earlier this year, Fernando averaged roughly 509 points per game — a figure Scrabble Victoria called a new national record for 2026. He went on to finish 10th in the Championship division at the Australian Nationals over Easter, competing against the country's top-ranked adult players, including world number one David Eldar.

"All the hard work paid off."

— Dineth Fernando, 2026 World Youth Scrabble Champion

Fernando's method is straightforward: he studies approximately 200 words a day from the official Scrabble dictionary, a practice he maintained throughout his transition from Sri Lanka to Australia and into the lead-up to the world championship.

South Asian Dominance on the Board

Fernando's victory continues a striking pattern of South Asian excellence at the World Youth Scrabble Championships. Sri Lankan players swept the podium in 2023 when Hivin Dilmith, Adheesha Dissanayake, and Kavindu Malawaraarachchi finished first, second, and third respectively. India's Madhav Gopal Kamath took the crown in 2025, and Pakistan's players have won five titles overall — more than any other country.

This year, India's Manchali — who finished second in the 2024 edition in Kalutara, Sri Lanka — added another podium finish to his résumé, cementing his status as one of the circuit's most consistent competitors. The strong showing by players of South Asian heritage underscores the deep Scrabble culture across the subcontinent and its diaspora communities in Australia, the UK, and North America.

A Rising Force in Australian Scrabble

Since arriving in Victoria, Fernando has earned recognition beyond the youth ranks. At the Victorian Championship, he won the Youth Prize and recorded the tournament's highest word — IDOCRASE, worth 149 points — a play that caught the attention of seasoned adult competitors. He also finished second at the 4th Wodonga Open, trailing only Nigeria-born Australian champion Ayorinde Saidu.

Karen Richards, Australia's national youth Scrabble coach, has worked with Fernando and other young Victorian players as part of a broader effort to develop the country's next generation of competitive Scrabblers.

The Sri Lanka High Commission in Canberra issued a statement congratulating Fernando, noting his achievement "brings tremendous pride to both Sri Lanka and Australia." The commendation highlighted the role diaspora communities play in bridging national identities through sport and intellectual competition.

What's Next

At 14, Fernando is eligible to compete in several more editions of the World Youth Scrabble Championship, which is open to players under 18. His rapid ascent — from Sri Lankan junior circuits to Australian national-level play to a world title in under a year — suggests the competitive Scrabble world may be watching him for some time to come.
